subject: Day 59: toy just out of reach
bodyText:
Today's focus
The post-vaccine window has closed and the easy stretch begins. With Avi engaging more and reaching emerging, today is about motivating the stretch-and-push toward 60-plus minutes of tummy time.

Action items
- Resume full tummy time toward 60-plus minutes per day cumulative, placing a toy just out of reach to motivate stretching and forearm push-ups. HealthyChildren tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Confirm the 4-month visit and its vaccines are on the calendar: window opens day 112 to 126 with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/
- If returning to work, use this calm stretch for a two-to-four-hour daycare or nanny trial run to test the handoff before leave ends.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Decreasing spit-up volume and longer alert windows as he engages more with faces and toys.
- [monitor] Persistent head turn to one side or a flattening spot (positional plagiocephaly); alternate his resting head side and add prone time.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting, a new color change during feeds, or feeding refusal lasting more than 24 hours.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, blue lips, labored breathing, or sudden limpness; for blue lips or trouble breathing call 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Let him track the toy fluidly side to side and up toward the midline as his visual following sharpens at this age. HealthyChildren baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Take an easy daylight stroller loop now that the vaccine window has passed; outdoor light and varied sensory input support his rhythm and your cardiovascular recovery. HealthyChildren vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Graduate read-aloud from purely high-contrast pages to a simple narrative or texture book to engage tactile attention alongside the visual. Reach Out and Read: https://reachoutandread.org/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens near three months; start a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit. Vaccines: RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.
- Watch for the first laugh in the coming weeks (typical range 10 to 14 weeks).

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
